proposals.before: Then Yue explained: "In all the realm only literary craft, the Changes, and chess matter—and you walk off with every one at once; that is stinginess indeed."
proposals.after: Then Yue explained: "Under heaven there are only literary meaning, chess, and calligraphy—and you have carried them all off at once; that may indeed be called greed."
proposals.reason: 文義棋書 lists literary meaning/arts, chess, and calligraphy or writing; it does not refer to the Changes.

proposals.reason: 文義棋書 lists literary meaning/arts, chess, and calligraphy or writing; it does not refer to the Changes.

proposals.before: If Bo Yi alone had held the western river, would anything have been accomplished?
proposals.after: If Shu Qi alone had held the western river, would anything have been accomplished?
proposals.reason: Chinese 叔齊 is Shu Qi, not Bo Yi (伯夷); the English invents the wrong brother.

proposals.after: Had Shu Qi alone guarded the western river, could the affair have succeeded?

decisions.after: Then Yue explained: "In all the realm only literary arts, chess, and calligraphy matter—and you walk off with every one at once; that is stinginess indeed."
decisions.reason: 文義棋書 is literary arts, chess, and calligraphy (書), not the Changes (易); the proposal rightly drops 易 but wrongly turns 不廉 into "greed"—s0008's tease already renders 不廉 as stinginess/ungenerous.

decisions.after: Yue then said: "Under heaven there are only literary arts, chess, and calligraphy—yet you carry them all off at once; one might call that ungenerous indeed."
decisions.reason: 書 in 文義棋書 is calligraphy/writing, not the Changes; keep 不廉 as ungenerous (matching s0008), not "greedy."
次子閏，司徒掾 names the office 司徒掾, a clerk to the Minister over the Masses (司徒), not a secretariat clerk.
司徒掾 is clerk to the Situ (Minister over the Masses); "clerk in the Secretariat" invents a 尚書 office not in the Chinese.
向使叔齊守于西河 names 叔齊 (Shu Qi); Bo Yi would be 伯夷 and is not in this unit.
Chinese has 叔齊, not 伯夷; the literal must read Shu Qi.
元後之付王莽 is Empress Yuan entrusting Wang Mang; "Yuandi's heir" invents an heir and misreads 後.
元後 is Empress Yuan, parallel to 二世 as the trusting party; not Yuandi's successor.
